flags.description: command that prints a JSON array of agent sessions (cwd, id, name, status, updatedAt, resume) to show how to resume each piece of work; default $SPECSYNC_SESSIONS_CMD; an empty value disables it for this run; it does not run with -state=off. Taken only from here or the environment, never from a repository file

flags.name: sessions-timeout
flags.description: how long to wait for the session provider

flags.name: state
flags.description: on (default), fresh to bypass the request cache, or off for local facts only (then only work whose head is in the base is recognised)

safety_rules: Dry run by default: nothing is removed unless -apply is given

A worktree is a candidate only when its work is provably in the base (its request merged with this head, or the head is in the base) and its tree is clean; a request closed without merging is never a candidate

Never removes a dirty tree, a worktree with ignored files other than common build output (unless -include-ignored), unpushed commits, an open request, a protected branch (main, master, develop, trunk, staging, production, prod, gh-pages, release/*, hotfix/*, cleanup.protect globs, the base or default branch, or the one checked out in the main checkout) or a branch with commits from several authors, the current worktree or the main checkout
Live sessions protect a worktree only when a session provider is configured and answers; otherwise the dry run warns and -apply refuses unless -assume-no-sessions is given

Each candidate is checked again from fresh facts just before it is touched, in this order: hooks (in the main checkout with SPECSYNC_WORKTREE set, 60 s limit; an item whose hooks cannot run because the config is not trusted is skipped), remove the worktree, delete the local branch only if its tip is still the verified head (the result says how to restore it), delete the remote branch; a failed hook leaves the worktree and branch in place
The remote branch is deleted only when its upstream is the same remote and branch name, its tip, read now, is the head being removed, and no open request targets it
A dry run writes nothing: no git objects (no merge prediction) and no request cache; a config with problems makes the items skip, never fall back to defaults
Never archives a change or touches the tracker: when cleanup.archive is true and the issue is closed it prints the specsync archive command as a follow-up

spinoff.description: Spin off emergent work from a discovery.

flags.name: change
flags.description: child change slug (default: derived from text)

flags.name: dry-run
flags.description: show what would be written without modifying files

flags.name: from
flags.description: parent change slug (required)

flags.name: kind
flags.description: issue kind: bug, followup, or task (sets label)

flags.name: openspec
flags.description: path to the openspec/ directory

flags.name: repo
flags.description: target repo as owner/name (default: same as parent)

flags.name: store
flags.description: registered OpenSpec store id to operate on (default: openspec/config.yaml `store:`, else ./openspec)

flags.name: task
flags.description: task index to spin off (1-based); omit for free text mode

flags.name: text
flags.description: discovery text (required when -task is not set)

safety_rules: Either -task or -text required
Creates a new change locally
Link the changes with specsync link after
examples: specsync spinoff -from my-change -text 'Found edge case in X'

status.description: Show where your current work stands, or every change with -everything.

flags.name: all
flags.description: include archived changes

flags.name: budget
flags.description: advisory size budget for the size flags, e.g. files=15,lines=400,commits=30 (default: the change's budget line, then $SPECSYNC_BUDGET, then built-in limits)

flags.name: change
flags.description: scope to one change (default: every change)

flags.name: everything
flags.description: list every change instead of the current work

flags.name: exclude
flags.description: glob of paths left out of the size counts (repeatable), e.g. go.sum

flags.name: json
flags.description: output as JSON

flags.name: openspec
flags.description: path to the openspec/ directory

flags.name: sessions-cmd
flags.description: command that prints a JSON array of agent sessions (cwd, id, name, status, updatedAt, resume) to show how to resume each piece of work; default $SPECSYNC_SESSIONS_CMD; an empty value disables it for this run; it does not run with -state=off. Taken only from here or the environment, never from a repository file

flags.name: sessions-timeout
flags.description: how long to wait for the session provider

flags.name: state
flags.description: on (default) reuses pull request data for up to a minute; fresh refetches it; off skips the tracker and pull request lookups: local git facts only, offline

safety_rules: Never modifies your worktree, index, refs or the tracker; it may write a short-lived request cache outside the repo, and git merge-tree may add unreferenced objects

sync.description: Synchronize an OpenSpec change with GitHub Issues.

flags.name: all
flags.description: sync every change in the resolved root (required to sweep a store)

flags.name: assignee
flags.description: board assignee login (default: the acting viewer, "me")

flags.name: change
flags.description: sync only this change (default: all changes)

flags.name: close-completed
flags.description: close the tracker item once every task in a change is checked

flags.name: dry-run
flags.description: print the provider commands and rendered body without executing

flags.name: force
flags.description: write to a closed issue instead of refusing (a closed issue is the strongest signal a cached ref is stale; an ambiguous marker match is never overridden here — use `specsync adopt` to disambiguate)

flags.name: labels
flags.description: add specsync/stage:<stage> labels to synced issues (off by default: neither is read back by specsync; a sync without this flag also removes them from issues that already carry them)

flags.name: mcp-config
flags.description: path to the MCP provider's config (used only with -provider mcp)

flags.name: openspec
flags.description: path to the openspec/ directory

flags.name: project
flags.description: target GitHub Projects board as owner/number (default: openspec/specsync.yml board; unset = no board)

flags.name: provider
flags.description: work provider: github, beads, mcp (repeatable; auto-detect when absent)

flags.name: reconcile
flags.description: merge external task state back into tasks.md before pushing

flags.name: repo
flags.description: target repo as owner/name (default: auto-detect from git remote)

flags.name: slices
flags.description: project each declared slice as a child issue of the change's issue, blocked by the slices it comes after; list them in the issue body when the provider cannot nest issues

flags.name: spec
flags.description: spec source: openspec (default) or beads

flags.name: status-map
flags.description: stage→Status overrides as stage=Name pairs, e.g. "active=In Progress,archived=Done" (default: $SPECSYNC_STATUS_MAP)

flags.name: store
flags.description: registered OpenSpec store id to operate on (default: openspec/config.yaml `store:`, else ./openspec)

safety_rules: Always use -dry-run first to preview changes
Always pass -change when one change is in scope (without it, syncs every change)
Confirm git remote points to the right repo

trace.description: Trace dependencies and relationships of a change.

flags.name: store

flags.name: until

trust.description: Allow specsync to run the commands in this repo's specsync.yml.

flags.name: dry-run
flags.description: with -yes, show what would be recorded without recording it

flags.name: openspec
flags.description: path to the openspec/ directory

flags.name: revoke
flags.description: remove the trust record for this repository

flags.name: yes
flags.description: record trust for the commands printed (without it nothing is recorded)

safety_rules: Without -yes it only prints the commands and records nothing; read them, then run the printed specsync trust -yes
Writes only a per-user record (a hash of the config) outside the repo
A changed config needs trust again; specsync never runs repository-defined commands without it

update.description: Bring your branch up to date with its base or upstream: a plan first, then -apply.

flags.name: apply
flags.description: run the plan (without it nothing changes)

flags.name: fetch
flags.description: run git fetch first so the plan sees current remote branches

flags.name: json
flags.description: output the plan as JSON

flags.name: openspec
flags.description: path to the openspec/ directory

flags.name: push
flags.description: with -apply, push afterwards (with a lease after a rebase)

safety_rules: Without -apply it prints the plan and changes nothing
Refuses a dirty working tree; never force-pushes a shared branch (those are merged)
Pushes only with -push, and after a rebase of a pushed branch only with --force-with-lease
Stops at a conflict, names the files and leaves git's own merge or rebase state for you to resolve or abort
The plan uses the sync: strategy from openspec/specsync.yml; run with -fetch to refresh remote branches first

flags.description: output as JSON

flags.name: store
flags.description: registered OpenSpec store id to operate on (default: openspec/config.yaml `store:`, else ./openspec)

safety_rules: Read-only operation
Run before syncing
